claims.statement: The Boundary meta-workspace declares six VCS-connected staging L3 workspaces in the rosa-boundary project: credentials, account, two networks and two regional runtimes, all pinned to Terraform 1.16.0. Each network pair and runtime pair reuses a source working directory while retaining separate workspace state.

The staging AWS-credentials stack's default role group allowlists all six Boundary workspaces, including the west network and regional workspaces, and the Boundary meta-workspace binds its generated default AWS dynamic credentials variable set to each of them.
The AWS-credentials workspace binds a project-scoped TFE-token set alongside its generated AWS dynamic credentials set; the network, account and regional workspaces bind only the generated AWS set.

All twelve current L3 workspaces in the L2 map set auto_apply = true and auto_apply_run_trigger = true except rosa-boundary-prod-aws-creds, which is the only workspace that explicitly sets auto_apply = false and auto_apply_run_trigger = false (combined with execution_mode = "remote"). Staging's six workspaces reach auto_apply = true either explicitly (rosa-boundary-stage-network-us-west-2, rosa-boundary-stage-account, rosa-boundary-stage-regional, rosa-boundary-stage-regional-us-west-2) or by inheriting the called module's default (rosa-boundary-stage-network, rosa-boundary-stage-aws-creds). Production's five non-credentials workspaces (rosa-boundary-prod-account, rosa-boundary-prod-network-us-east-1, rosa-boundary-prod-regional-us-east-1, rosa-boundary-prod-network-us-west-2, rosa-boundary-prod-regional-us-west-2) all set it explicitly while keeping execution_mode = "remote", so only the production credentials bootstrap workspace requires manual apply confirmation.

Both regional workspaces receive their own VPC and private-subnet IDs as explicit Git-managed L2 variables; the current map does not transfer network outputs through remote state or declare network-to-regional source-workspace run triggers.

The Boundary meta-workspace calls version 0.0.23 of the private TFE workspaces module to declare notifications, Git-managed variables and variable-set bindings; this single module call now declares all twelve current L3 workspaces -- six staging workspaces in the rosa-boundary-stage AWS account (rosa-boundary-stage-network, rosa-boundary-stage-network-us-west-2, rosa-boundary-stage-aws-creds, rosa-boundary-stage-account, rosa-boundary-stage-regional, rosa-boundary-stage-regional-us-west-2) plus six production workspaces mirroring the identical topology in the separate rosa-boundary-prod AWS account (rosa-boundary-prod-aws-creds, rosa-boundary-prod-account, rosa-boundary-prod-network-us-east-1, rosa-boundary-prod-regional-us-east-1, rosa-boundary-prod-network-us-west-2, rosa-boundary-prod-regional-us-west-2).

The AWS-credentials provider is guarded to staging account 150100906299 and its TFE provider targets hp-platform-engineering; its default role group allowlists six Boundary project workspaces, while Trusted Actions is configured in a separate role group. Network and regional providers independently enforce allowed_account_ids guards.

A single account L3 workspace owns shared IAM identities, common managed-policy attachments including investigation-reaper VPC execution, user OIDC providers, the Bedrock budget and model agreements, independently of regional resource states.

The separate rosa-trusted-actions credentials role group allowlists global and stage workspaces and adds a secret-pattern-scoped secretsmanager:GetSecretValue policy to its plan role alongside ReadOnlyAccess, without adding that permission to Boundary's default plan group or overriding the apply-role policy defaults.

Both staging regional workspaces use the same rosa-boundary-stage role prefix and us-east-1 legacy_policy_region; the regional naming rule keeps east inline-policy names unsuffixed and appends -us-west-2 in west, so distinct regional grants accumulate on shared account roles rather than isolating their permissions.

Staging's account input explicitly approves us-east-1 and us-west-2 for the shared Bedrock logging role; the role retains SourceAccount restriction and permits only the configured regional SourceArn patterns, while invocation-log destinations and delivery grants remain regional.

The meta-workspace's L2 map defines a second, separate AWS account bootstrap: rosa-boundary-prod-aws-creds and rosa-boundary-prod-account target AWS account 514903006123, distinct from the staging account 150100906299, via their own provider guard, cloud.tf workspace name, and generated dynamic-credentials module instance.

The production credentials stack's default role group now allowlists all six registered production workspaces (rosa-boundary-prod-aws-creds, rosa-boundary-prod-account, rosa-boundary-prod-network-us-east-1, rosa-boundary-prod-regional-us-east-1, rosa-boundary-prod-network-us-west-2, rosa-boundary-prod-regional-us-west-2); its inline comment about authorizing workload workspaces 'separately after registration' predates this, since all four workload workspaces (both regions' network and regional stacks) already appear in the list. The L2 map defines a full two-region production topology mirroring staging -- rosa-boundary-prod-network-us-east-1/regional-us-east-1 and rosa-boundary-prod-network-us-west-2/regional-us-west-2 -- and, unlike rosa-boundary-prod-aws-creds, rosa-boundary-prod-account plus all four of these network/regional workspaces set auto_apply = true, so only the credentials workspace still requires manual apply confirmation before a run actually applies.

rosa-boundary-prod-account reuses the deploy/account working directory with production-specific Git-managed variables: role_name_prefix = "rosa-boundary-prod", stage = "prod", aws_account_id = "514903006123", legacy_policy_region/legacy_role_tag_region both "us-east-1", bedrock_logging_source_regions set to ["us-east-1", "us-west-2"] for both now-live production regions, and adopt_existing_resources = false reflecting a greenfield account. Unlike rosa-boundary-prod-aws-creds, this workspace sets auto_apply = true and auto_apply_run_trigger = true.

The production account's rosa-boundary-prod-network-us-east-1 and rosa-boundary-prod-regional-us-east-1 workspaces reuse deploy/network and deploy/regional respectively: the network workspace uses us-east-1a/b defaults matching staging's east region, and the regional workspace sets account_role_name_prefix="rosa-boundary-prod" and legacy_policy_region="us-east-1" as its own legacy-naming owner, with concrete vpc_id/subnet_ids values annotated as a "T3-PR6 (#408)" network-apply output. Both workspaces set auto_apply = true and auto_apply_run_trigger = true (unlike rosa-boundary-prod-aws-creds), and a mirrored us-west-2 network/regional pair (rosa-boundary-prod-network-us-west-2, rosa-boundary-prod-regional-us-west-2) now completes the same two-region topology staging already has.

rosa-boundary-prod-regional-us-west-2 mirrors the staging west regional workspace's self-contained pattern: it sets account_role_name_prefix = "rosa-boundary-prod", keeps legacy_policy_region = "us-east-1" (never designating itself a second legacy owner, so its inline policies take the -us-west-2 suffix), carries concrete vpc_id/subnet_ids values annotated as a "T3-PR8 (#428)" network-apply output, and sets its own bedrock_model_agreements, claude_default_model, container_image/lambda_image_repository/lambda_image_tag pins, and log_retention_days = 90, with auto_apply = true and auto_apply_run_trigger = true.
